messages:
Ken: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector change from v2 to v3 we're seeing memory spikes in continuous-batching runs that lead to intermittent OOMs on p3.2xlarge. Profiling attached in thread.

Maya: Seen it too, hit a canary at ~3000 concurrent tokens where batch growth jumps unexpectedly.

Oliver: Any idea which kernel path? cuBLAS algos can pick bigger workspace.

Ken: Yeah, initial flamegraph points to attention kernel picking a temp-space-heavy algo for certain seq lengths >1024. Also our allocator arenas are fragmented so peak RSS is higher.

Sasha: Repro steps? I can run a narrow test harness.

Ken: Repro: run continuous-batch harness with seq distribution [8, 16, 64, 512, 1024, 1536] and 32 concurrent streams. Command: ```./perf_harness --mode=continuous --seq-mix=... --streams=32 --kernel-selector=v3``` Logs show KV cache reserved ~= 2.1GB, workspace high-water ~= 6.4GB on a 16GB card.

Priya: OOMs + high padding = two problems: kernel workspace and padding waste from batch padding to max-seq in batch. Need per-seq overhead accounted in batch accounting.

Oliver: Proposed quick fixes: (1) force kernel algo selection to mem-constrained for v3, (2) shrink default workspace cap from 512MB -> 256MB per-thread, (3) add buffer-reuse map keyed by (dtype, size) to avoid new allocations each step. Thoughts?

Maya: +1 to buffer-reuse. We should also subtract reserved KV cache from the allocator's available pool so the allocator doesn't overcommit. Right now allocation logic treats KV as ephemeral.

Ken: Ran experiment: forced mem-safe kernel + buffer reuse -> OOMs dropped 90%, but observed 8% throughput regression due to slower kernel algos.

Sasha: That's expected. We need smarter kernel scoring: include estimated temporary memory footprint in score alongside compute time. If a bigger-workspace kernel yields marginal speedup but huge mem, prefer smaller mem one when headroom low.

Priya: For continuous batching accounting, propose adding a per-sequence fixed overhead of 128 bytes * seq_len (or maybe per-attn-row) plus a per-stream constant 1MB for stream state. This reduces batch growth surprise.

Oliver: Also found allocator fragmentation stems from many different-sized temp allocations from fused kernels. Slab allocator for small temps (<=64KB) and large-size pool with size-buckets for >64KB looks promising.

Ken: Quick perf note: enabling slab reduced peak allocations by ~22% in synthetic test. But we still see padding waste: large outlier seqs cause whole-batch pad.

Maya: Could we do dynamic minibatching inside a batch: group by seq-length into sub-batches at runtime? That reduces pad but increases scheduling complexity. Worth prototype.

Priya: Another mitigation: KV evictions for cold streams. If KV cache holds cold contexts we can evict older keys to reclaim headroom — tradeoff for some cache miss latency.

Sasha: Actionable plan: 1) add kernel-memory to selector scoring (Oliver), 2) implement buffer-reuse map + slab allocator (Maya), 3) change allocator cap to account for KV reserved (Ken), 4) prototype intra-batch grouping by seq-length (Sasha), 5) add per-seq overhead to batch accounting and test (Priya).

Oliver: I'll file PR for kernel-scoring change with flag `--prefer-mem-safe`.

DevBot: CI check for eng-runtime/kernel-selector PR #812 passed on ubuntu-gpu-1 (logs: /ci/812). :white_check_mark:

Maya: I'll start buffer-reuse patch, aim to land prototype by EOD tomorrow.

Ken: Thanks — let's sync tomorrow 11am to review telemetry and decide whether to backport mem-safe mode to current deploy.

Priya: One more note — add telemetry metric: \"workspace_high_water\" per-device per-deployment + \"pad_waste_bytes\" per-batch, so we can compute unit-cost impact.

Oliver: Agreed. That will help decide trade-offs between latency and cost.

Ken: Great thread. If anyone hits regressions locally, ping me in #eng-runtime with `oom-debug` tag.
